## Set-up
```{r}
library(readxl)
library(tidyverse)
library(ggplot2)

```


## Datasets
```{r}
filipino_stats <- read_xlsx("C:/Users/pikmi/Documents/MetroState/25 Data 211 (Data Science)/Data Project/Mika, Izzy - Stats tracking - DRAFT 2 - remove extra info.xlsx")
```


## Data clean-up

```{r}

# Clean up data 
filipino_stats <- filipino_stats %>%
  filter(Keep==1) %>%                     #Keep tracked words (ignore eg function words, proper nouns)
  group_by(Day) %>%                       #Group by day / get numbers per day
  summarize(
    day_count = n()                       #Total words per day
    ,Y_count = sum(Correct_YN == 'Y')     #Total correct answers per day
    ,N_count = sum(Correct_YN == 'N')     #Total incorrect answers per day 
    ,percent_Y = (sum(Correct_YN == 'Y')/day_count)    #Percent correct
    ,percent_N = (sum(Correct_YN == 'N')/day_count)    #Percent incorrect     
     
  )

# Data - Removing Day 8, 9, 10
#---------------------------------
# Didn't realize this until later - the video used for part of 8/10 
#   (and all of 9) interviews people mostly speaking Bisaya(/Binisaya), which is 
#   a related but diff language that I haven't studied before/was not studying  
#   via the course I had. Removing from final data set to avoid wonky results.

tagalog_stats <- filipino_stats %>%
  filter(Day < 8 | Day > 10)


#tagalog_stats
#tagalog_stats$Y_count
#tagalog_stats$percent_Y


```

## Prop Test - Comparing Correct vs Incorrect Answers

I want to see if studying Tagalog via the LearningTagalog course for 20 min every day (over 14 days) increases the percentage of words I understand over time when reading/watching conversational Tagalog. 

I'm using prop testing to test whether the proportion of correct answers is significantly greater than proportion of wrong answers. 

$P_Y$ - Proportion of correct answers ("Y")

$P_N$ - Proportion of incorrect answers ("N")

$H_0: P_Y = P_N$

$H_a: P_Y > P_N$


```{r}
# Test - is proportion of correct answers greater than proportion of wrong answers?
# Sum all Ys, sum all Ns, see if Y > N

allY <- sum(tagalog_stats$Y_count)
allN <-sum(tagalog_stats$N_count)
totalWords <-allY+allN

prop.test(x=allY, n=totalWords, alternative = "greater")


```

## Conclusion
With a $p-value = 2.2e{-16} < 0.05$, then with $5\%$ significance level, the null hypothesis can be safely rejected; which supports the hypothesis that the number of words I understood is higher than the number of words I got wrong. This combined with a line graph shows a mild positive trend over time / an increase in words understood over time. 

## Plots

```{r}

# Plot percentage of words understood per day as a line graph.
p <- ggplot(data = tagalog_stats, aes(x = Day, y = (percent_Y * 100)))+
  geom_line(color="#225BC9")+
  labs(title = 'Percent of Words Understood Per Day', x = 'Day', y = '% Words Understood')

p <- p + ylim(0,100)

p


# Plot total number of correct words vs incorrect words as a bar graph.
df <- data.frame(Words = c("Correct", "Incorrect"), Count =c(allY, allN))

p2 <- ggplot(df, aes(x=Words, y=Count))+geom_bar(stat="identity", aes(fill=Words))+labs(title="Total Words Correct vs Incorrect over 11 Days", x= "Words Encountered")

p2
#plots show a small but clear positive trend


```
